title: Bomb Kills Three and Injures 21 at Upscale Moscow Restaurant Near Kremlin
excerpt: A woman carrying an improvised explosive device detonated it near an Italian restaurant in a Stalin-era skyscraper, killing a security guard, a customer, and herself.
body:
• Three people died and at least 21 were injured when a homemade bomb exploded near the Balzi Rossi restaurant on Moscow's Kudrinskaya Square on Saturday evening.
  • The dead include the woman carrying the device, a security guard who stopped her, and a restaurant customer; 17 of the injured are in serious condition.
  • The upscale Italian restaurant was hosting a private banquet reportedly attended by senior Russian military and political figures, including Deputy Defence Minister Yunus-Bek Yevkurov.
  • Authorities have not identified the bomber or disclosed a motive; Russia's Anti-Terrorism Committee and FSB are leading the investigation.

A homemade bomb carried by an unidentified woman killed three people and injured at least 21 near the Balzi Rossi restaurant in central Moscow on Saturday evening, according to Russia's National Anti-Terrorism Committee, cited by state news agency RIA Novosti.

The explosion occurred around 8:10 p.m. local time on Kudrinskaya Square, at the base of one of Moscow's iconic "Seven Sisters" Stalinist skyscrapers. The restaurant, an upscale Italian establishment, was closed to the public for a private banquet at the time of the blast.

What Happened

The woman attempted to enter the restaurant but was stopped by a security guard before she could reach guests on the outdoor terrace, the Anti-Terrorism Committee said. The device detonated at the entrance, killing the guard, the woman, and a restaurant customer.

Russian business daily Kommersant reported that the apparent targets were guests attending a private event on the terrace. The newspaper cited sources suggesting the bomb may have been detonated remotely, raising the possibility that the woman did not know she was carrying an explosive device.

"There were people lying on stretchers, a young woman was hysterical."

— Eyewitness at the scene

Emergency services, police, and a bomb disposal team were deployed to the landmark residential building. Roads around Kudrinskaya Square were briefly closed.

High-Profile Guests

Reports from multiple Russian media outlets, including war propagandist Anastasia Kashevarova, indicated that the restaurant was hosting members of Russia's political and military elite. Numerous vehicles with black military-issue license plates were observed outside the venue.

Among the reported guests was Russian MP Zelimkhan Mutsoev, whose Maybach was seen at the scene, and Deputy Defence Minister Yunus-Bek Yevkurov, who recently turned 63. It has not been officially confirmed whether the event was a birthday celebration for a senior general.

Security Context

The attack is the most significant bombing in central Moscow in years. Russia's FSB security service said earlier in 2026 that it would step up protection for high-ranking military officials following a series of assassinations and attempted killings that Moscow has blamed on Ukraine.

The 2023 assassination of military blogger Vladlen Tatarsky at a St. Petersburg café, in which a bomb concealed in a statuette killed the blogger and wounded 42, drew comparisons from Russian commentators. In that case, Ukraine's involvement was later indirectly confirmed by a senior security official.

Authorities have not drawn any links between Saturday's blast and the ongoing Russia-Ukraine conflict. No group has claimed responsibility.

What Comes Next

Russia's Investigative Committee has opened a criminal probe into the explosion. The identities of the victims have not been released. Balzi Rossi chef Carmine Alfieri posted on social media that his staff were safe, describing the incident as "a minor issue" — a characterization at odds with the scale of the casualties. The restaurant remains closed pending the investigation.
